justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-sloping trajectory from roughly 341.5 at one day out to 347 at one month, suggesting I was anchoring primarily on recent price momentum and a mild bullish bias in the near-term trend. At the one-day horizon, the estimate stays close to the last observed price, since very short-term forecasting is dominated by mean-reversion tendencies and the assumption that overnight or intraday drift will be limited. Moving out to one week and one month, I incorporated a slight upward drift assumption, consistent with a market environment where broader equity indices have been grinding higher and where this asset class tends to track that general direction over intermediate horizons.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, which is a standard reflection of compounding uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 23 points, which accounts for normal daily volatility, potential intraday news surprises, and liquidity-driven price swings. By one month, the interval widens to 85 points, acknowledging that macroeconomic data releases, central bank communications, earnings reports, and shifts in risk appetite can all materially alter the trajectory over a four-week window. The asymmetry around the point estimate is relatively modest, reflecting no strong skew signal at the time of the forecast.

The primary tail risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include a sudden repricing of Federal Reserve rate expectations, either from a surprise inflation print or an unexpected shift in Fed guidance, which has historically been a major driver of sharp moves in this asset class. A broader risk-off event, such as a geopolitical escalation, a credit market disruption, or an unexpected deterioration in economic data, could push the outcome well below the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected resolution of macro uncertainty or a significant liquidity injection could push prices above 390.

It is worth emphasizing that these forecasts carry meaningful uncertainty even within the stated intervals. Financial time series are prone to regime changes and volatility clustering, meaning that calm periods can give way to turbulent ones with little warning. The stated intervals should be interpreted as probabilistic guideposts rather than hard boundaries, and the actual outcome falling outside them would not be surprising — roughly one in ten outcomes is expected to do so by construction.
